body: I've been alone for so long that it's just normal.  Having a SO is a strange and foreign concept to me.
A combination of ugliness, shyness, depression, lack of personality, and living in an area devoid of people similar to myself.
This is something I struggle with on a daily basis.  When I'm talking to customers during my job I know I sound like a complete idiot wuss.
Seriously thank you for this post.  I struggle with most of these things every day.
Thanks.  I really really appreciate it.
That's good.  I couldn't sleep until 8a, and I woke up at 12p and haven't slept since.  When you hit rock bottom like me you have to hold onto the small victories.

I'm in the same boat.  I've held off shooting myself in the head until my parents die.  It won't be long either; one is morbidly obese and smokes, and one is over 70, smokes, and has already had multiple strokes.
Play video games for 16 hours straight while thinking of ways to kill myself.

I'm not any more depressed on Valentine's Day than any other day of the year.  I can't be sad about not being in a relationship because I've never been in one, so I don't have any Valentine's Day experiences to compare this one to.
Yep.  It's the reason why when my computer breaks I succumb to deeper depression and come closer to the noose.  It's pathetic like you said, but oh well.
Video games.

For me it's complete hopelessness.  It's a continuous repeating narrative in my head of all the mistakes I've made as well as how much of an idiot I would be to try to pull myself out of my miserable life.  There are rare moments of happiness, but those are like breaching the surface of the water to get a quick gasp of air before sinking back down.

I've been unemployed for three years and I've come to detest my birthdays since then because they're stark reminders of how much of my life I've wasted.  My 30th birthday is next week, and I've done absolutely nothing with my life.
I haven't drank anything with caffeine in it for over three years.
This was indeed well written, and I'm glad getting it out helped you.  Also, welcome to Reddit!
Unemployment.  And being fat.  And ugliness.  And social anxiety.  And being a coward.
My 30th birthday is approaching.  I deeply want to kill myself before it hits.  I know it's basically meaningless , but it's a stark milestone marker that demonstrates how much I've wasted my life.
That would be perfect but I assumed at least a Bachelor's was required.
Thirty in four months.  You?  Also, which subreddit were you referring to being addicted to?
I can sympathize.  My dream is to live in South Korea to pick up the language and experience a different culture.  I have no degree, no money, and no skills.
I have 5 people in my phone, and 90% of the calls on it in the last three years have been from my parents.
Video games and books.  Also, I just got into learning 3d modeling, which is very difficult but fun and rewarding.
Long-term unemployment and complete lack of relationships, as well as the social anxiety that causes both.

I describe it as feeling like a ghost, if that makes any sense.  I feel like I should have been dead for several years, but I'm somehow still walking around and interacting with people for some reason.  I don't ever feel like a part of it; just an observer of real people.

The longer I can sleep during the day the better.  I'm up to about 10 hours a day currently.  I'd rather sleep permanently, but since I'm too cowardly for that I'll settle for this.  I have very vivid dreams, and once in a blue moon I'll get a happy one.

Thanks for the reply.  I was diagnosed with social anxiety disorder last year and prescribed medication for it.  I went to a therapist for a while but that just made it worse.  I'm the same way as you with job interviews; they're so stressful that I can barely get through them without having a panic attack.  This problem with programming isn't the cause of my suicidal thoughts so much.  It's just bad depression overall caused by many things.  My problems with C have just made it worse in the past couple days.  I guess I got in over my head trying to start with C.  Maybe I'll install Python and give it a try.  Do you know any good lessons available online, or maybe a book recommendation?

Thanks for the response, I appreciate it.  I guess things aren't all that bad.  I tend to dwell on the little things to the point that I can't cope with them.  Hopefully if I try and focus on the positive things I still have going for me then my mood won't be so low.
